elements.element: Audit frequency limited to once per 12 months / once per year
elements.evidence: "may, no more than once per year and upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice"

elements.element: At least 15 days' prior written notice
elements.evidence: "no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company" (exceeds the 15-day floor)

elements.element: Vendor bears the cost of the audit (subject only to an underpayment >10% exception)
elements.evidence: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI." — no cost-shift exception, which is more favourable to Customer

elements.element: No more than once per 12 months

elements.evidence: "thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company"

elements.element: Audit performed by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality
elements.evidence: "HDI's General Manager ... have the right to inspect the records" — audit by Vendor's own personnel, no independence or confidentiality undertaking
"fees incurred by HDI ... shall be borne by HDI" — unconditional Vendor cost, at least as protective

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: clause grants a right to "inspect the records of the Company's General Manager" with no express bar on direct system access

reasons: The locked fallback level is fully satisfied: the inserted "no more than once per year" supplies the missing frequency cap, the existing 30 days' notice exceeds the 15-day fallback floor, and HDI unconditionally bears its own inspection costs (better than the >10% underpayment carve-out).

Preferred is not reached because there is no requirement for an independent auditor bound by confidentiality and no express prohibition on direct access to Customer systems; these are preferred-only refinements and correctly left alone at the locked fallback.
Minimal: a single short insertion of an operative frequency limiter into the existing sentence, no rewrite, no new exception, no boilerplate.
Intent preserved: notice, business-hours limitation, scope of records and cost allocation are untouched, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
Margin comment is accurate and non-operative; it correctly states the clause otherwise sits at the fallback.
